findings.title: Node buffs are re-applied each refresh but never removed or downgraded when a node dies or the player leaves radius
findings.problem: The buff loop only ever calls addPotionEffect with a freshly computed amplifier; there is no removePotionEffect / amplifier-lowering path anywhere in NodeSystem (grep over the whole mechanics package finds removePotionEffect only in PlayerGoodsManager and MultiArenaManager). Two consequences: (a) when a player leaves buffRadius or the last node is destroyed, the effect survives for the full configured buff-duration-ticks instead of ending with the buff source; (b) Bukkit's addPotionEffect does not replace an existing effect with a weaker one, so when activeNodeCount drops (a node dies), the previously granted higher amplifier keeps ticking out its duration while applyBuffsToPlayer keeps computing a lower one. Symmetry is broken: apply is per-tick, removal is never done.
findings.impact: Players keep node speed/resistance/regeneration for up to buff-duration-ticks after the node is gone or after they walk out of range, and the amp level ratchets upward within a fight and only decays by expiry. With the GUI-exposed buff-duration-ticks set above buff-refresh-ticks this becomes a permanent free buff; it also makes 'destroy the node to remove the buff' untrue, which is core tower-defense feedback.
findings.trigger: Player stands in buffRadius during a wave, then a node is destroyed (damageNode) or the player moves out of range; next applyAllBuffs tick recomputes a lower/zero amplifier but the old effect keeps running.

findings.title: Journal is retained forever and the arena is wedged in ENDING when the world is not loaded at reset time
findings.problem: On the not-loaded path restoreWithResult returns false before `journals.remove(worldName, journal)` (line 540) and before any RestoreOperation is created, so the per-world journal is neither drained nor dropped and no active restore exists to retry it. Callers treat `false` as terminal: ArenaInstance.reset() logs 'reset blocked ... run /hilltop disable then /hilltop enable to retry' and leaves state ENDING, while the journal (up to MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_PER_WORLD = 1,000,000 OriginalBlock records) plus journalOverflowWarned/journalTruncated entries stay reachable for the remaining process lifetime. Nothing re-drives restore for that world except the onDisable sweep restoreAllNow().
findings.impact: A single unloaded/renamed arena world (Multiverse unload, world deleted during a reset, multiverse reload) permanently wedges that arena in ENDING with no automatic retry, and retains an arbitrarily large block-snapshot map (~140-170 bytes/entry per the class's own estimate) for the rest of the uptime. The only recovery is a full server restart, which loses the journal entirely and leaves the map half-modified.
findings.trigger: Arena reset (ArenaInstance.reset -> restoreWithResult) while definition.getWorldName() is not currently loaded, e.g. /hilltop disable handled after the world was unloaded, or a world reload plugin reloading the arena world mid-END.

findings.title: Node repair interaction handler lacks ignoreCancelled, so a denied right-click still consumes repair items
findings.problem: Every other handler in this class declares ignoreCancelled = true (onBlockBreak line 103, onEntityExplode 114, onBlockExplode 124, onBlockExplosionDamage 145), but the repair handler is registered at NORMAL with no ignoreCancelled and never tests event.isCancelled(). A PlayerInteractEvent already cancelled by a region/protection/adventure-mode plugin still reaches the repair branch at lines 208-247: planRepair() is computed, repairNode() heals the node, and item.setAmount(...)/setItemInMainHand(null) consumes the repair item, while the interaction itself was denied. The handler then calls event.setCancelled(true) on an already-cancelled event, so nothing signals the inconsistency.
findings.impact: On servers with any protection plugin (WorldGuard regions, claim plugins) or in worlds where the arena block interaction is denied, players can repair nodes and lose repair items through a click the server refused; conversely, a protection plugin that cancels earlier in the chain cannot actually block node repair.
findings.trigger: Right-click a RESPAWN_ANCHOR node with a repair item while another listener at LOWEST/LOW/NORMAL-earlier has already cancelled the PlayerInteractEvent.

findings.title: ItemsAdder reflection swallows the root cause, then logs a misleading 'not installed' warning per hammer
findings.problem: The catch block discards the exception object entirely (`catch (Exception ignored)`) and emits a fixed message that asserts the plugin is missing. ClassNotFoundException, NoSuchMethodException (ItemsAdder API changed), IllegalAccessException and InvocationTargetException (CustomStack.getInstance returned null so getItemStack NPEs) are all collapsed into the same text with no class name, no stack trace, and no distinction from the iaPlugin == null branch at line 142 which falls through silently. Because createHammer() is called for every hammer given out, a broken ItemsAdder API produces an unbounded stream of identical misleading warnings and a silent fallback to the vanilla axe.
findings.impact: Admins cannot tell 'ItemsAdder not installed' from 'ItemsAdder installed but API incompatible / item id wrong'; the configured custom hammer model silently degrades to a vanilla IRON_AXE (getHammerMaterial default) with no actionable diagnostic, and log spam grows with every hammer crafted.
findings.trigger: Any createHammer() call (shop purchase, /hilltop hammer, starter kit) with hammer.use-itemsadder=true and a bad item id or a changed ItemsAdder API version.

findings.title: Preview villagers whose chunk unloaded are dropped from the tracking list without being removed from the world
findings.problem: Both clearAll() (line 127-134) and clearInWorld() (line 112-124) only call remove() on entities for which isValid() is true, then unconditionally drop every reference. A preview villager whose chunk was unloaded has isValid() == false while the entity body is still stored in the region file, so the onDisable path (HilltopVillagePlugin line 309 `villagerPreviewManager.clearAll()`) loses the only handle to it. The startup reaper cleanupOrphans() also iterates world.getEntities(), which only returns entities in loaded chunks, so it cannot see them either; recovery depends entirely on onEntitiesLoad firing later. Because spawnPreview sets setPersistent(true) and setRemoveWhenFarAway(false) (lines 101-102) these entities are written to disk.
findings.impact: Invulnerable, no-AI, persistent preview villagers can survive /hilltop reload ... plugin disable and the following server restart in an unloaded chunk, reappearing when an admin or player later loads that chunk; until onEntitiesLoad runs they are ordinary villagers with the preview PDC and are not covered by any in-memory cleanup path.
findings.trigger: Wizard step 5 previews exist, their chunk unloads (admin walks far away / world unload), then the plugin is disabled or the server restarts.

unverified: NodeAttackGoal/ExplodeBeetleGoal double-counting of node damage could not be confirmed without reading the full goal tick paths (only attackNode/damageNode call sites were inspected).
Whether ArenaScoreboard.getAliveCount() shows 0/3 when protected villagers sit in unloaded chunks (isValid() false) was not verified end-to-end.
Interaction between MapRestoreManager's MONITOR ordering and any third-party explosion-block plugins in this server's plugin list was not tested.
notes: MapRestoreManager is heavily hardened (per-tick batching, failure requeue, truncation flag consumed in complete(), disable barrier via restoreAllNow/restoreNow): no correctness defect in journal capture/restore of twice-changed blocks or multi-block explosions was found; the residual issue is the not-loaded-world path (S07-F2) which retains the journal and wedges the arena. NodeListener/NodeSystem otherwise guard null PlayerData and use isRegisteredActive identity checks consistently. HammerListener/FireballListener cooldown and BossBar maps are UUID-keyed with quit/cleanup paths; only the reflection error handling is reported.
